segments.text: > Part of the [Implementation Status](README.md) index. Node's `path` module — portable filesystem path manipulation. Import-gated (`import path from 'path'` or `import { join } from 'path'`) — see [TDD-00049](../tdd/TDD-00049.md)/[ADR-00141](../adr/ADR-00141.md)/[ADR-00142](../adr/ADR-00142.md).

notes: Joins with `/`, then normalizes (collapses repeated slashes, drops `.` segments, resolves `..` against segments already seen in the same call)

Absolute-always: starts from `process.cwd()`, walks segments left to right, any segment starting with `/` resets the accumulator (discarding everything before it, including cwd) — equivalent to real Node's right-to-left "stop at the last absolute segment" algorithm
Directory portion; trailing slashes trimmed first

Final path segment, optionally with a trailing `ext` stripped — not stripped when doing so would consume the whole segment, unless the *entire* `path` argument equals `ext` (then returns `""`), matching real Node's own asymmetric rule here
Extension of the basename, including the leading `.`; `""` for a dotfile whose only `.` is its first character
`parse` returns `{root, dir, base, ext, name}`; `format` is the inverse (`base` wins over `name`+`ext`, `dir` falls back to `root`)

caveats: POSIX-only (this compiler doesn't cross-compile) — the compile-time constants `/` and `:`, never the Windows `\`/`;` forms
notes: No cross-compilation, so no Windows form is ever needed — see [process.platform](PROCESS-CLI.md)
